title: Example HarborFresh Case Practice
description: Original synthetic exercises for a fictional local meal-kit company.

structuringPrompts.title: Diagnose a margin decline
structuringPrompts.situation: HarborFresh grew orders this year, but operating margin fell from 12% to 7%.
structuringPrompts.objective: Identify the drivers of the margin decline and the highest-value corrective action.

hypotheses.label: Fulfillment and ingredient costs grew faster than revenue.
hypotheses.rationale: The hypothesis links the margin decline to measurable revenue and cost drivers.

hypotheses.label: Customer demand collapsed across every plan.
hypotheses.rationale: Total orders increased, so a broad demand collapse is inconsistent with the known fact.

branchOptions.label: Revenue and mix
branchOptions.description: Review order volume, prices, discounts, and plan mix.

branchOptions.label: Cost base
branchOptions.description: Review ingredient, packaging, labor, delivery, and fixed costs.

modelStructure.title: Revenue and mix
questions: Did discounts or plan mix reduce revenue per order?

modelStructure.title: Cost base
questions: Which unit costs grew faster than order volume?

brainstormingPrompts.title: Improve subscriber retention
brainstormingPrompts.context: First-month cancellations rose after HarborFresh changed its menu and delivery windows.
brainstormingPrompts.question: Which actions should the team test first to improve retention?

ideas.label: Offer pause and delivery-window choices before cancellation.
Remove dietary preferences from account settings.
Track cancellation reasons by menu and delivery window.
Wait for one annual survey before changing service.

synthesisPrompts.title: Recommend a kitchen expansion
synthesisPrompts.situation: The current kitchen is near capacity, while demand differs sharply by neighborhood.
synthesisPrompts.decision: Recommend whether HarborFresh should lease a second kitchen this quarter.
facts: The east neighborhood has enough committed demand to use 80% of a small kitchen.
A six-month lease option costs 20% more per month but limits long-term downside.

recommendation.label: Use the six-month option for a small east kitchen.
Sign a five-year lease for a large citywide kitchen.

evidence.label: The finance office is also in the east neighborhood.

risk.label: Committed demand may weaken after launch.
The kitchen exterior may need a different paint color.

nextStep.label: Verify commitments and negotiate volume gates before signing.
Sign the long lease before checking customer commitments.

synthesisPrompts.modelClose: HarborFresh should use the six-month option for a small east kitchen because committed demand supports 80% utilization. The main risk is demand decay, so the team should verify commitments and negotiate volume gates before signing.

knowledgeCheck.explanation: Contribution per box equals $18 minus $12, or $6.
knowledgeCheck.prompt: A box sells for $18 and has $12 of variable cost. What is contribution per box?

lessons.objective: Connect price and variable cost to contribution per unit.
principles: Contribution per unit equals price minus variable cost per unit.
Use contribution, not revenue, to cover fixed costs.
lessons.title: Calculate contribution per unit

workedExample.prompt: A box sells for $20 and has $12 of variable cost.
steps: Subtract $12 of variable cost from the $20 price.

fitPrompts.prompt: Tell me about a time you improved an important operating result.
followUps: How did you identify the opportunity?
How did you measure the result?

fullCases.title: Neighborhood pickup rollout
fullCases.situation: HarborFresh tested pickup points in two neighborhoods and must decide where to expand next quarter.

structure.title: Structure the pickup decision
structure.situation: Pickup adoption and unit economics differ between the east and west pilots.
structure.objective: Determine whether and where to expand neighborhood pickup.

hypotheses.label: Expand east first if contribution and repeat demand remain attractive.
hypotheses.rationale: This is a market-specific hypothesis tied to measurable economics and demand.

hypotheses.label: Expand both neighborhoods because each pilot attracted some users.
hypotheses.rationale: Any adoption is not enough to establish attractive economics.

branchOptions.label: Demand
branchOptions.description: Assess adoption, repeat use, and addressable order volume.

branchOptions.label: Economics
branchOptions.description: Assess contribution, setup costs, and break-even volume.

modelStructure.title: Demand
questions: Which neighborhood has durable pickup adoption?

modelStructure.title: Economics
questions: Which pilot generates enough contribution to cover setup costs?

exhibit.title: Pickup pilot performance
exhibit.description: Average weekly results from the final month of each pilot.

questions.prompt: What weekly contribution does the east pickup pilot generate?

explanation.short: Multiply eligible orders by adoption and contribution per pickup order.

brainstorming.title: Improve pickup performance
brainstorming.context: HarborFresh can run two tests before the next rollout decision.
brainstorming.question: Which actions should HarborFresh test to improve demand and economics?

ideas.label: Target east customers with high repeat meal-kit use.
Launch pickup citywide before another test.
Test pickup hosts that use existing staffed counters.
Build dedicated pickup buildings in every neighborhood.

synthesis.title: Recommend a pickup rollout
synthesis.situation: East produces stronger adoption and contribution than west.
synthesis.decision: Recommend the next pickup rollout step.

recommendation.label: Expand east selectively and hold west.

evidence.label: East produces four times west's weekly contribution.
Both pilots use the HarborFresh brand.

risk.label: East adoption may not persist after the pilot offer ends.
HarborFresh may move its accounting office.

nextStep.label: Run a four-week east retention test before adding sites.
Sign long leases across the city immediately.

synthesis.modelClose: HarborFresh should expand pickup selectively in east and hold west because east produces four times the weekly contribution. The main risk is whether demand persists, so the next step is a four-week east retention test.
